The gas turbine diagnostic system is designed for simulation and control of gas turbine units, protection and simulation of automatic control functions, and adjustment and stabilization of process variables.
The simulation model reflects the main functionality and dependencies between the essential characteristics and key parameters of the gas turbine process.
The simulation system can be used to create optimal schedules for equipment operation according to a production plan.
The three-level hierarchy of the simulation system includes SCADA software, PLC software, and VISSIM simulation software.
The lower level VISSIM simulation models pressure and temperature sensors, lube and seal oil pumps, cooling fans, and other field equipment.
The transfer functions for the gas turbine model were identified by analyzing data from a real GTK 10i gas turbine unit at the Chizha compressor station.
The simulation system can be used to test and debug the control algorithms for the gas turbine main and auxiliary equipment, as well as the SCADA system functionality.
The simulation model was developed using version 5.0 of the VISSIM (Visual Simulation) software package.
The paper references literature on prediction models, foreign gas turbines, energy equipment maintenance, mathematical modeling, and gas compression station maintenance.
The gas turbine diagnostic system has a modular software architecture with three hierarchical levels.
The system can be used to train compressor station personnel on the principles of operation of the gas turbine control system.
The simulation model was developed based on analysis of data from a real GTK 10i gas turbine unit.
Dynamic Data Exchange (DDE) protocol is used to transmit data between the hierarchical levels of the simulation system.
The simulation system can be used to test and optimize the software for gas turbine automation systems.
The adequacy of the mathematical model to the real gas turbine process is a critical factor for successful diagnostics and optimization.
